extracted.intended_audience: research authors, peer reviewers and editors considering or participating in eLife's peer-review process
extracted.subtask_description: Description of eLife's policies and expectations for peer review of preprints, including who makes decisions, what outputs are produced, and constraints on reviewer/editor requests. Intended to guide authors, reviewers and editors interacting with eLife's 'publish, then review' model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint-only review
rubrics_metrics.description: We only review research papers that have been made available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife is creating a system in which we only peer review articles that are available as preprints; this combines the immediacy and openness of a preprint with the scrutiny and curation of a peer-reviewed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions by active researcher editors
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions are made by editors who are active researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are taken by practicing researchers (editors) rather than administrative staff, emphasizing expert judgement in evaluating submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial acceptance-rate limits
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we publish or have a set acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is not governed by a target acceptance rate; publication is based on assessment of the work rather than quota-based constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative review discussion before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers discuss their reviews with each other before reaching a decision on a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors engage in discussion to reconcile viewpoints and ensure coherent decision-making; this collegial discussion informs the final editorial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraint on requests for additional work
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra experiments, analyses, or data collection are only requested if they are essential and can be reasonably completed within about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers/editors should limit requests for further work to what is essential and feasible within a short timeframe (approx. two months); see the 'Publishing in the time of COVID-19' guidance for related context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual editorial outputs: public comments and detailed author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Our editorial process produces two outputs: i) public comments from the peer reviewers on the strengths and weaknesses of the work, and whether the authors’ claims and conclusions are justified by their data; ii) detailed feedback on the manuscript for the authors, including requests for revisions and suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments are intended for readers and posted alongside the preprint; detailed feedback is intended to help authors revise and improve their preprint and may be published with the paper if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments must include evaluation summary and individual public reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The public comments include an evaluation summary that captures the major conclusions of the review process, and public reviews from each of the peer reviewers that outline the strengths and weaknesses of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation summaries capture major conclusions; individual reviewer reports are published publicly to increase transparency of the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of decision letter and author response for accepted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted manuscripts published in eLife include the decision letter from the editor to the authors, and the author responses to the decision letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For revised preprints that are accepted, detailed feedback and the author response are published as part of the paper to increase transparency about the revision process and editorial reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment based on peer reviews, not journal title
rubrics_metrics.description: Research is primarily assessed on the basis of reviews from peers and not on the title of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife emphasizes assessment by expert reviewers over prestige metrics or journal-brand signals, aligning with principles to reduce journal-based evaluation bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Impact Factor as an evaluative tool and DORA support
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor and is a co-founder of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal endorses responsible research assessment practices and publicly rejects reliance on the Impact Factor when evaluating research or researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and measurement of editorial process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in our Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and others can consult published metrics about the editorial process (e.g., timelines, outputs) to understand and evaluate eLife's practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall aim: faster, fairer, more open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall aim is to make peer review faster, fairer and more open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle underpins the described policies (preprint review, public comments, transparent outputs, editorial discussion, limited additional work requests).
